types.statement: The API identifies a site-to-site IPSec peer by one of four credential types: CN (certificate common name), UFQDN (VPN user FQDN), IP (VPN IP address) or XAUTH. UFQDN and IP need a VPN_SITE_TO_SITE subscription, the CN type is created automatically when Zscaler provisions a CN, UFQDN is the most common, and the type cannot be changed after creation.

expect.description:
VPN is one way to route traffic from customer locations to the cloud. Site-to-site IPSec VPN credentials can be identified by the cloud through one of the following methods:

  1. Common Name (CN) of IPSec Certificate

  2. VPN User FQDN - requires VPN_SITE_TO_SITE subscription

  3. VPN IP Address - requires VPN_SITE_TO_SITE subscription

  4. Extended Authentication (XAUTH) or hosted mobile UserID - requires VPN_MOBILE subscription

 Notes:

 IPs must be created in Static IP first

 CN type (certificate) is created automatically, when a CN is provisioned by Zscaler.

 The 'psk' field is not applicable for this VPN type.

 The most common type is UFQDN.

VPN authentication type (i.e., how the VPN credential is sent to the server). It is not modifiable after VpnCredential is created.

Note: Zscaler no longer supports adding a new XAUTH VPN credential, but existing entries can be edited or deleted using the respective endpoints.

xauth-legacy.statement: Zscaler no longer supports adding a new XAUTH VPN credential; existing ones can be edited or deleted. The console's Authentication Type choices for adding are FQDN and IP; each takes a pre-shared key.

quotes: Zscaler no longer supports adding a new XAUTH VPN credential, but you can edit or delete the existing entries from the Zscaler Admin Console.
You can edit or delete an existing XAUTH VPN credential from the Zscaler Admin Console. However, you cannot add a new XAUTH VPN credential.
Choose the Authentication Type that is used to identify the peer, and configure it accordingly:
New Pre-Shared Key: Enter a pre-shared key. The pre-shared key can be up to 255 characters.
New Pre-Shared Key: Enter the pre-shared key. The pre-shared key can be up to 255 characters.

ip-from-static-ip.statement: An IP-type credential's address must already exist as a static IP; the console's drop-down lists only the static IPs provisioned for the organization, and Zscaler provisions them on request.

expect.description:
Static IP address for VPN that is or provisioned by Zscaler. This is a required field for IP auth type and is not applicable to other auth types.

Note: If you want Zscaler to provision static IP addresses for your organization, contact Zscaler Support.

quotes: The static IP addresses that appear in the drop-down menu are the addresses that are provisioned for your organization.

immutable.statement: Neither the credential type nor, once set, its FQDN (UFQDN) or IP address (IP) can be changed on update: the Python SDK rejects the attempt, and the Terraform resource marks `type`, `fqdn` and `ip_address` ForceNew, so a change deletes and recreates the credential.

expect.description:
VPN authentication type (i.e., how the VPN credential is sent to the server). It is not modifiable after VpnCredential is created.

Note: Zscaler no longer supports adding a new XAUTH VPN credential, but existing entries can be edited or deleted using the respective endpoints.

psk-required.statement: A pre-shared key is required for UFQDN and IP credentials; the Terraform resource marks it sensitive and forces replacement when it changes, and the data source's read-back is commented out.

tenant-limit.statement: A tenant can hold up to 16,000 VPN credentials, and the console can import or delete many at once from a CSV.

quotes: You can add up to 16,000 credentials.
Import or delete multiple VPN credentials for different authentication types using a CSV file to reduce the configuration effort for the administrator.

csv-import.statement: A VPN credential CSV import takes up to 3,000 entries per file and can add and delete credentials of different authentication types in one file. VPN user IDs are converted to lowercase on import. Import Results should show nothing under Failed Records; if a credential was not properly added or deleted, the file must be re-imported.

quotes: You can import up to 3,000 entries per CSV file.
VPN User IDs are automatically converted to lowercase after import.
Ensure that nothing appears under Failed Records. If a credential (or record) was not properly added or deleted, you must re-import the file.
You can use one CSV file to add or delete VPN credentials for different authentication types.

csv-xauth.statement: By CSV, an existing XAUTH VPN credential can be deleted (-) but a new one cannot be added (+).

quotes: You can delete (-) an existing XAUTH VPN credential but cannot add (+) a new VPN credential using the CSV file.

csv-fields.statement: Each CSV row has Action (+ or -), PSK Type, VPN User Name (for FQDN, a valid user ID that does not end in a period, and whose special-character rule, including "@", is the divergence ufqdn-at-sign; for IP, the local gateway address sent to Zscaler beforehand), Comment (at most 10,240 characters) and Pre-Shared Key (or XAuth password, depending on the PSK Type).

quotes: Action (Required): Enter + or - to indicate whether you want to add or delete a VPN credential.
PSK Type (Required): Enter the proper authentication type for the VPN credential:
The proper user ID of the FQDN. It must be valid and cannot include special characters (e.g., <, @, [], etc.) or end in a period (e.g., safemarch.).
The IP address of your local gateway. This is the address that you sent to Zscaler beforehand.
Comment: Enter additional notes or information. The comments cannot exceed 10,240 characters.
Pre-Shared Key (Required): Enter the pre-shared key or XAuth password, depending on the PSK Type entered.

csv-fields.conditions: The page's rule on special characters in an FQDN user ID, including "@", conflicts with its own example; that part is left to the ufqdn-at-sign divergence. The PSK Type values (UFQDN, IP, XAUTH) are too short to quote one by one.

csv-managed-by.statement: Managed_By names the SD-WAN partner managing the credential, or is a comma when none manages it; the valid partner names listed include Cisco Viptela, Citrix SD-WAN, CloudGenix, HPE Aruba, Riverbed SteelConnect, Silver Peak and VMware VeloCloud.

quotes: Managed_By: If this VPN credential is being managed by an SD-WAN partner, enter the name of the partner. If the credential is not being managed by a partner, enter a comma instead. The valid partner names are:
Cisco Viptela
Citrix SD-WAN
CloudGenix
HPE Aruba
Riverbed SteelConnect

csv-managed-by.conditions: The list has an eighth partner name, "ngena", too short to quote alone; hence "include".

ufqdn-at-sign.summary: The CSV import rule says an FQDN user ID cannot include special characters such as "@", but the same page's example row and the Juniper SSG 20 guide use a user@domain form.

quotes: The proper user ID of the FQDN. It must be valid and cannot include special characters (e.g., <, @, [], etc.) or end in a period (e.g., safemarch.).

positions.says: An FQDN user ID must be valid and cannot include special characters such as <, @ or [] or end in a period.

quotes: +,UFQDN,jane.doe@example.com,My example FQDN VPN Credential,12345,,

positions.says: The example UFQDN row uses jane.doe@example.com as the user ID.

quotes: Local ID: Enter the FQDN for the VPN credentials you added in the Zscaler Admin Console. In this example, it's the FQDN example@safemarch.com.

positions.says: The SSG 20 guide's example FQDN for the VPN credentials is example@safemarch.com.

ufqdn-at-sign.impact: An import following the rule could not carry the user@domain form the examples use. The rule may mean the part before the "@", but the page does not say so.

psk-live-read.title: Whether a live tenant returns preSharedKey on GET /vpnCredentials
psk-live-read.detail: The API contract lists preSharedKey in the GET response and the Go SDK struct carries it without a not-returned note, while the Terraform provider never reads it back. Whether the live service populates it is unverified (was clarification shared-38). Compare a GET against a tenant with a known credential; the secret-bearing-API reasoning is in shared.terraform.credential-handling.

cn-certificate-specifics.title: Certificate-based IPSec authentication through the CN credential
cn-certificate-specifics.detail: Unverified legacy statement: Certificate-based auth via the CN type is implied but specifics are not confirmed by any capture, and CN and XAUTH are legacy types not recommended for new deployments. No captured source states it; Zscaler Support or a vendor article would settle it.
